title: Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program 2026: Six-Week Foreign Policy Fellowship for Congressional Staff
summary: The Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program (CFP) is a six-week professional development fellowship designed for current Congressional staff who want to deepen their understanding of global affairs, debate major foreign policy issues, and connect with leading experts and policymakers. The programme brings together Congressional staffers from across the political aisle and creates an environment where participants can exchange ideas, examine complex international issues, and develop stronger professional networks. About the Congressional Fellowship Program The Wilson Center s Congressional Fellowship Program focuses on foreign policy, global affairs and the legislative process . Throughout the six-week seminar, Fellows engage with leading foreign policy thinkers and practitioners. Sessions are designed to encourage analytical thinking, fresh perspectives and informed debate around important international issues. The programme also includes an interactive simulation intended to encourage Fellows from across the political aisle to network, collaborate and work together . What Does the Fellowship Offer? Selected Fellows will participate in a structured six-week seminar covering key global and foreign policy issues. The programme provides opportunities to: Debate major international and foreign policy issues. Engage with leading foreign policy experts and practitioners. Develop analytical approaches to complex global issues. Gain fresh perspectives through discussions and recommended readings. Network with Congressional staff from across the political aisle. Participate in an interactive simulation. Connect with policymakers, academics and executives through the Wilson Center community. Certificate of Completion Fellows are expected to attend the majority of the programme sessions. Participants who attend at least five of the six sessions will receive a certificate of completion from the Wilson Center . Successful Fellows will also become part of the Woodrow Wilson Congressional Fellowship Alumni Network . Access to the Wilson Center Alumni Network One of the long-term benefits of the programme is continued access to the Wilson Center s alumni community. The programme has an alumni network of approximately 1,000 members , providing Fellows with opportunities to maintain professional connections after completing the programme. Alumni may also be invited to participate in exclusive Wilson Center opportunities, including: Private briefings Study trips around the world High-level roundtables Other Wilson Center events and activities Alumni can also draw upon the expertise of Wilson Center experts, including policymakers, academics and executives from both the public and private sectors. Who Is the Fellowship For? The Congressional Fellowship Program is specifically designed for mid- to senior-level Congressional staff . Applicants should: Be current Congressional staff . Have a strong understanding of the legislative process. Have an interest in foreign policy. Aspire to pursue or continue a career focused on shaping foreign policy. Be able to attend at least five of the six required sessions. The programme is therefore not presented as a general fellowship open to students, recent graduates or members of the general public. Programme Schedule The provided information lists the following six sessions: September 18 September 25 October 2 October 16 October 23 October 30 The sessions take place on Fridays from 2:30 p.m. to 5:00 p.m. at the Wilson Center or on Capitol Hill. Applicants should only apply if they are confident that they can meet the required attendance commitment. Spring and Fall Sessions The Wilson Center states that it hosts two Congressional Fellowship Program sessions each year , one in the spring and one in the fall. The provided announcement states that applications for the Fall 2026 session are now open . It also contains a separate reference stating that applications for Spring 2026 are open. Because the supplied information contains both references, applicants should check the official application page for the session and dates currently accepting applications. How to Apply Interested Congressional staff should submit their application through the Wilson Center s application portal. APPLY HERE Applicants should carefully review the programme requirements and make sure they can attend the required sessions before applying. Application Deadline The information provided does not specify an application deadline for the Fall 2026 session. Applicants should therefore check the official application page for the current deadline and any additional application requirements before submitting their application. Visit HERE to learn more about the Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program 2026 Conclusion The Wilson Center Congressional Fellowship Program provides current Congressional staff with an opportunity to strengthen their understanding of foreign policy while engaging directly with experts, policymakers and fellow Congressional professionals. Through its six-week seminar, interactive discussions, cross-aisle networking and alumni opportunities, the programme can help Congressional staff develop the knowledge and professional relationships needed to contribute more effectively to foreign policy discussions. However, applicants should note that the programme is specifically intended for current Congressional staff , particularly those at the mid- to senior-level who have an understanding of the legislative process and an interest in shaping foreign policy.. title: Pinterest Apprenticeship Program: A Pathway Into Technology for Non-Tech Professionals
summary: The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program provides professionals from non-technical backgrounds and individuals who may face barriers to entering the technology industry with an opportunity to gain practical experience at Pinterest. The programme is designed for people looking to transition into technology while gaining hands-on experience in areas including engineering, product management, product design and product research . About the Pinterest Apprenticeship Program Entering the technology industry can be difficult for people who did not begin their careers in traditional technology roles. Pinterest s apprenticeship programme provides an alternative pathway for professionals who want to develop relevant skills and gain experience within a technology company. The programme specifically aims to support people from non-tech backgrounds and individuals who may have experienced barriers to entering the industry. Rather than requiring everyone to follow the same traditional career path, the programme creates opportunities across several areas of technology and product development. Apprenticeship Opportunities Available The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program features four main pathways: 1. Apprentice Engineer The Apprentice Engineer pathway provides an opportunity to gain experience in software engineering and technology development. Depending on the position, apprentices may be exposed to: Software development Engineering projects Technical problem-solving Working with engineering teams Development processes Technology products and systems This pathway can be suitable for professionals who have developed technical skills through alternative education or career routes and want to transition into a professional engineering environment. 2. Apprentice Product Manager The Apprentice Product Manager pathway focuses on developing and improving digital products. Product management involves understanding user needs, identifying opportunities and working with different teams to guide product development. Apprentices may gain experience in: Product strategy User needs and research Product development Cross-functional collaboration Problem identification Product decision-making This pathway may be particularly relevant to people with backgrounds in business, strategy, communications, project management or research. 3. Apprentice Product Designer The Apprentice Product Designer pathway focuses on creating digital products and user experiences. Participants may gain experience in: Digital product design User experience User interface design Design thinking Problem-solving Working with product and engineering teams This can provide an entry point into technology for professionals with design or other creative backgrounds. 4. Apprentice Product Researcher The Apprentice Product Researcher pathway focuses on understanding users and using research findings to inform product decisions. Areas of exposure may include: User research Research methodologies User behaviour Data and insights Product decision-making Collaboration with designers, engineers and product managers This pathway may be relevant to people with backgrounds in research, psychology, sociology, social sciences, communications and related disciplines. APPY HERE How Long Does the Apprenticeship Last? Pinterest states that apprenticeships can last for up to one year . However, the exact length of an apprenticeship is not guaranteed. Participants are employed throughout the programme, and apprentices may potentially be considered for conversion to a full-time role at Pinterest after completing the apprenticeship. It is important to note that full-time employment is not guaranteed . Who Is the Programme Designed For? The programme is particularly focused on: Professionals from non-tech backgrounds Individuals seeking to transition into technology People who may have experienced barriers to entering the technology industry Candidates interested in engineering, product management, product design or product research Individuals looking for an alternative pathway into the technology sector This makes the programme especially interesting for career changers who already possess transferable skills but need practical technology industry experience. What Can Apprentices Gain? An apprenticeship can provide an opportunity to develop both technical and professional capabilities while working in a real-world environment. Participants can potentially build: Industry knowledge Technical and professional skills Practical work experience Professional networks Understanding of technology development Confidence working with cross-functional teams These experiences can help participants become better prepared for future technology roles. Visit HERE to learn more about the Pinterest Apprenticeship Program Potential Pathway to Full-Time Employment One of the major attractions of the programme is the possibility of being considered for a full-time position at Pinterest. However, applicants should understand that conversion is not guaranteed . The apprenticeship should therefore be viewed primarily as a professional development and work experience opportunity, with potential for longer-term employment depending on available roles and the individual s performance. A Supportive Professional Community Pinterest also highlights its focus on building a community where employees can develop relationships, connections and a sense of belonging. For apprentices, being surrounded by colleagues and professionals can be particularly valuable when making a career transition into a new industry. How to Prepare for the Programme Although the next application opening has not been given a specific deadline, prospective applicants can start preparing now. 1. Choose Your Career Path Consider whether you are most interested in: Engineering Product management Product design Product research 2. Highlight Transferable Skills Coming from a non-tech background does not mean you have no relevant experience. Skills such as communication, research, problem-solving, project management, data analysis, creativity, business strategy, customer understanding and leadership can be valuable in technology roles. 3. Build Relevant Projects Start creating evidence of your skills. For example: Engineering candidates can build software projects. Product management candidates can create product case studies. Designers can develop UX/UI portfolios. Product researchers can showcase research projects and user insights. 4. Research Pinterest Learn about Pinterest s products, users and technology. Understanding the company s platform can help demonstrate genuine interest when applications open. 5. Sign Up for Updates Pinterest is encouraging interested candidates to sign up for apprenticeship notifications so they can receive updates when applications open for the next cohort. Application Deadline No specific application deadline has been announced for the next cohort. Interested candidates should sign up for notifications and monitor Pinterest s official apprenticeship channels for the next application opening. Conclusion The Pinterest Apprenticeship Program offers an alternative route into the technology industry for professionals who may not have followed a traditional technology career path. title: External Fellowship 2027–2029: Digital Justice Initiative Fellow in Washington, DC
summary: The Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law is inviting applications for an Externally Funded Fellowship 2027–2029 with its Digital Justice Initiative in Washington, DC. This fellowship offers an exciting opportunity for an emerging legal professional committed to racial justice, civil rights, privacy, and emerging technology to work at the intersection of law and technology. The fellow will have the opportunity to identify emerging legal and policy challenges while also developing strategies to hold corporate and government actors accountable through litigation and advocacy. About the Digital Justice Initiative The Digital Justice Initiative focuses on the intersection of racial justice, technology, and privacy. The initiative addresses issues including exploitative data practices, discriminatory algorithms, privacy violations, disinformation, and online hate, particularly where these practices disproportionately affect communities of color. Fellows will participate in substantive legal work, including co-counseled litigation with prominent law firms. Their responsibilities may include client contact, case investigation, discovery, negotiations, amicus briefs, appeals, and trial practice. They may also contribute to legislative and public policy advocacy, legal services, and public education on civil rights issues. Fellowship Focus Areas The fellowship may focus on one of two primary areas: 1. Surveillance Pricing The project may examine surveillance pricing including concerns surrounding data privacy, discrimination, and the collection and exploitation of sensitive personal information. 2. Generative AI The fellow may explore discrimination in generative AI tools, expanding civil rights research beyond traditional algorithmic decision-making systems and examining how emerging AI technologies may affect communities of color. The Lawyers’ Committee is also open to considering proposals that align with its mission and priorities but fall outside these specific focus areas. What the Fellow Will Do The selected fellow may: * Conduct factual and legal research on relevant technologies and practices. * Engage with affected communities, scholars, practitioners, and organizations. * Help shape litigation and advocacy strategies. * Develop cases challenging discriminatory practices. * Participate in implementing strategies developed during the fellowship. * Contribute to litigation and legal advocacy. * Support public policy and legislative advocacy. * Participate in public education on important civil rights issues. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should meet the following requirements: * Hold a JD or anticipate receiving a JD by May 2027. * Demonstrate a strong commitment to civil rights and racial justice. * Demonstrate creativity and initiative in developing and implementing civil rights projects. * Have prior experience working with or ties to low-income communities of color. * Have strong research, writing, and analytical abilities. * Be able to work collaboratively with staff, clients, and community organizations. * Have effective written and oral communication skills in legal and non-legal settings. * A computer science or other technology background is preferred. Application Requirements Interested candidates should submit: * Project Proposal– Including the proposed project s objectives, timeline, target populations, and expected outcomes. * Resume * Personal Statement – Describing relevant experience and qualifications. * References – Contact information for at least two professional or academic references. Salary and Benefits The fellowship is externally funded and will commence only if outside fellowship funding is secured. For an attorney receiving their JD in 2027, the expected salary is $76,000 . If the external fellowship award is lower than the Lawyers’ Committee salary scale, the organization will provide an additional amount to bring the fellow up to the appropriate salary. Benefits include: * Medical, dental, and vision healthcare coverage * Parental leave * 403(b) employer contributions and matching * Short- and long-term disability options * Employer-paid monthly cell phone stipend Fellowship Details Position: Fellow Programme: Digital Justice Initiative Organization: Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights Under Law Location: Washington, DC Duration: 2027–2029 Job Type: Term Expected Salary: $76,000 Level: Entry Level How to Apply Applicants should prepare their project proposal, resume, personal statement, and professional or academic references before submitting their application. Apply here: Find the link to the application form HERE . Applicants are encouraged to develop a proposal that clearly demonstrates their commitment to racial justice and explains how their proposed project can contribute to the Digital Justice Initiative s work. Conclusion The Digital Justice Initiative Fellowship 2027–2029 presents an opportunity for an emerging attorney to work on pressing questions surrounding civil rights, racial justice, privacy, surveillance pricing, and generative AI. For candidates with a JD who are passionate about using legal advocacy to address technology-related discrimination and advance racial justice, this fellowship offers the opportunity to combine research, litigation, community engagement, and policy advocacy to create meaningful impact. title: 1–2 PhD Positions in the DECENT Project at Lund University, Sweden
summary: The Department of Human Geography at Lund University is inviting applications for 1–2 PhD positions in Human/Economic Geography under the ERC-funded DECENT project (Socio-technical Modularity and the Decentralization of Infrastructure). The selected PhD students will be employed within the DECENT project and affiliated with CIRCLE (Centre for Innovation Research). The positions are particularly suitable for candidates interested in economic geography, innovation studies, socio-technical transitions, sustainability transitions, geography of innovation, and urban experimentation. About the DECENT Project Cities have traditionally depended on centralised infrastructure systems to provide essential services such as electricity, water, transportation, food, and finance. However, large-scale network-based infrastructures can struggle to adequately address changing social, economic, and environmental needs. The DECENT project examines how decentralized infrastructure solutions can provide societal functions in more modular ways. Examples of decentralized infrastructure being studied include: * Micro-grids * Small-scale wastewater treatment systems * Multi-modal transport * Short food chains * Distributed finance The project investigates how these decentralized solutions can overcome the historical legacies of large-scale infrastructure systems. Researchers will approach decentralization from a configurational socio-technical perspective , examining areas including local and global industry dynamics, the geography of innovation, sustainability transitions, and urban experimentation. The empirical research will compare infrastructure decentralization across cities in both high-income regions, such as Europe and North America, and middle-income regions, including South and Southeast Asia. PhD Research Opportunity The positions are based within the Department of Human Geography at Lund University and form part of the interdisciplinary DECENT research project. Successful candidates will have the opportunity to conduct doctoral research connected to the project s broader themes while developing expertise in areas such as: * Economic and human geography * Innovation studies * Socio-technical transitions * Sustainability transitions * Geography of innovation * Urban experimentation * Infrastructure decentralization * Local and global industry dynamics The positions may be particularly attractive to applicants interested in understanding how cities can transition from centralised infrastructure systems toward more distributed and modular alternatives. Who Should Apply? The opportunity is suitable for candidates with academic and research interests related to human geography, economic geography, innovation studies, socio-technical transitions, sustainability, infrastructure, cities, and urban development. Applicants should carefully review the official vacancy announcement for the complete eligibility requirements, required qualifications, application documents, and other conditions of employment. About Lund University Lund University is a major research university in Sweden with a broad international research environment. The PhD students will be based in the Department of Human Geography and affiliated with CIRCLE, the Centre for Innovation Research. Working within the DECENT project will provide doctoral researchers with an opportunity to contribute to research examining some of the major challenges surrounding infrastructure, innovation, sustainability, and urban transformation. How to Apply Interested candidates should review the full vacancy announcement and submit their application through Lund University s official recruitment portal. Number of Positions: 1–2 PhD positions Field: Human/Economic Geography Project: DECENT – Socio-technical Modularity and the Decentralization of Infrastructure Funding: European Research Council (ERC) Institution: Lund University, Sweden Deadline: August 28, 2026 Application Link Apply here: https://s-tep.org/job-opportunity-1-2-phd-positions-in-the-decent-project/ Applicants are encouraged to review the complete job description and application requirements before submitting their applications. Conclusion The DECENT PhD positions at Lund University offer an opportunity for aspiring researchers to contribute to an ERC-funded project exploring how cities can rethink the way essential services and infrastructure are organised. Candidates interested in economic geography, innovation, sustainability transitions, socio-technical systems, and urban experimentation are encouraged to explore the opportunity and apply before the August 28, 2026 deadline. title: Cherie Blair Foundation for Women Mentoring Programme 2026 in India
summary: The Cherie Blair Foundation for Women has opened applications for a new 12-month mentoring cohort exclusively for women entrepreneurs in India. The programme offers selected women entrepreneurs the opportunity to work with an experienced business mentor who can provide guidance, expertise and support to help them develop their businesses and achieve their professional goals. Through the Mentoring Women in Business programme, participants are matched with business professionals from around the world and work together online to identify goals, address business challenges, strengthen skills and develop practical strategies for business growth. The programme is designed to provide women entrepreneurs with access to personalised mentoring, new perspectives, professional networks and valuable business knowledge. About the Cherie Blair Foundation for Women Mentoring Programme The Mentoring Women in Business programme is a global initiative of the Cherie Blair Foundation for Women that connects women entrepreneurs in low- and middle-income countries with experienced business professionals. The programme is delivered online and provides one-to-one mentoring over 12 months. Mentees and mentors work together to create a plan focused on the entrepreneur’s business and personal development goals. The Foundation reports that among mentees graduating in 2024, 99% gained business skills, 96% applied improved business management practices, 94% progressed towards their business objectives, and 86% improved their business outcomes. What the Mentoring Programme Offers Selected women entrepreneurs will have the opportunity to: * Receive personalised one-to-one mentoring from an experienced business professional. * Work on specific personal and business development goals. * Strengthen business management and professional skills. * Gain new perspectives and practical advice from their mentor. * Build confidence in making business decisions. * Expand their professional and business networks. * Work through challenges affecting their business growth. * Access the Foundation’s online mentoring platform and community. * Receive support from the programme team throughout the mentoring relationship. * Receive a certificate upon successful completion of the programme. Eligibility Criteria The opportunity is specifically open to women entrepreneurs based in India for this cohort. Applicants should generally: * Be a woman from and living in a low- or middle-income country. * Own and run a business, with at least 51% ownership or decision-making authority, or be preparing to launch a business within the next three months. * Have intermediate-level or higher proficiency in English, both written and spoken. * Be able to commit to the programme for 12 months. * Have reliable internet access and be able to meet with a mentor online. * Be willing to work with a mentor to develop business and personal development skills. * Complete the required training, feedback questionnaires and programme activities. * Commit to meeting with their mentor for a minimum of two hours per month. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women] How the Mentoring Works Once selected, participants will complete approximately 1.5 hours of pre-matching training before being paired with a mentor. The mentor and mentee will then work together through several stages, including getting to know one another, establishing goals, developing an action plan, working towards objectives and reflecting on progress. Meetings take place online, with participants expected to spend at least two hours per month with their mentor. The programme team also provides ongoing support throughout the mentoring relationship. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women] Who Should Apply? This opportunity is ideal for women entrepreneurs in India who are looking to grow their businesses, strengthen their entrepreneurial skills, overcome business challenges and benefit from the experience of an international business professional. Whether you are looking to improve your business strategy, strengthen your management skills, expand your network or work towards specific growth objectives, the mentoring relationship can provide personalised support throughout the year. Application Process Interested applicants should review the programme s selection criteria and commitments before completing the online application form. The application requires responses in English and takes approximately 15–20 minutes to complete, according to the Foundation s programme information. ([Cherie Blair Foundation for Women] How to Apply Applications are currently being promoted for the India cohort. Application Deadline: 4 September 2026 Applicants should complete the online application before the deadline and ensure that they meet all programme requirements. Application Link: [Apply for the Cherie Blair Foundation Mentoring Programme] For questions regarding the mentoring application, applicants can contact [mentoringintakes@cherieblairfoundation.org] Conclusion The Cherie Blair Foundation for Women Mentoring Women in Business programme provides women entrepreneurs with an opportunity to gain personalised guidance while working towards meaningful business and professional goals. For eligible women entrepreneurs in India, this 12-month mentoring opportunity can provide access to international expertise, practical business support, professional networks and a community of ambitious entrepreneurs. If you know a woman entrepreneur who is ready to take her business to the next level, encourage her to apply before the 4 September 2026 deadline. title: L’Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027: €100,000 for Leading Women Scientists
summary: The L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027 celebrate outstanding women scientists whose research is making major contributions to the advancement of Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science . Created in 1998, the International Awards are one of the flagship initiatives of the L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme. Every year, the programme honours five eminent women scientists from five regions of the world , recognising exceptional scientific achievement and the important role women play at the forefront of global research. The scientific disciplines recognised by the International Awards alternate each year between Life Sciences and Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science . For the 2027 edition , the awards focus on Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science. Each of the five selected laureates will receive an award of €100,000 . Please note that this opportunity is different from the L Oréal-UNESCO regional fellowships and Young Talents programmes. The 2027 International Awards are intended to recognise established, internationally distinguished women scientists rather than doctoral students or early-career researchers. About the L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards The L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme was created to recognise the achievements of women researchers and increase the visibility of women in science. Since the International Awards were launched in 1998 , a total of 142 endowments have been awarded. Through the programme, L Oréal and UNESCO seek to highlight women whose scientific work has contributed significantly to knowledge, innovation and scientific progress. For the 2027 cycle, the programme recognises excellence in: Physical Sciences Mathematics Computer Science Five women scientists will ultimately be selected, representing five major regions of the world. Who Can Be Considered? The International Awards are intended for eminent women scientists who have made important contributions to scientific advancement. Unlike programmes designed specifically for PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers or young scientists, the International Awards recognise highly accomplished researchers with significant scientific achievements. Candidates should have an outstanding record of research in areas falling within the 2027 award disciplines: Physical Sciences Eligible research may fall within disciplines connected to the physical sciences and related fields covered under the programme s official rules. Mathematics Women researchers whose work advances mathematical knowledge may be considered for the award. Computer Science Researchers making important contributions to computer science and related areas are also included in the 2027 scientific focus. Applicants and nominators should consult the official 2027 Rules and Regulations to confirm whether a candidate s specific scientific discipline falls within the eligible scope. Five Global Laureates One of the defining features of the L Oréal-UNESCO International Awards is their global reach. Each year, five laureates representing five regions of the world are selected. The programme is therefore designed to recognise scientific excellence across different geographical regions and strengthen the international visibility of women researchers. The five selected scientists will join an international community of previous L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science laureates. Selection Process Candidates are evaluated by a jury composed of internationally renowned scientific experts . The International Awards place scientific excellence at the centre of the selection process. The programme seeks women researchers whose work has made important contributions to scientific progress and who demonstrate the exceptional achievements associated with one of the world s leading international recognitions for women in science. According to the 2027 calendar, the final selection of candidates is expected to be completed by: 31 December 2026 What You Get Each of the five selected laureates receives: €100,000 The award also brings substantial international recognition through the global L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science programme. Beyond the monetary endowment, recognition through the programme can provide greater international visibility for the scientific work and achievements of selected laureates. The International Awards are designed to celebrate women working at the highest levels of scientific research and highlight their contributions to global scientific advancement. Key Programme Information Programme: L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027 Scientific focus: Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science Number of laureates: 5 Award per laureate: €100,000 Partner: UNESCO Programme established: 1998 Total endowments awarded since launch: 142 Final selection: 31 December 2026 How to Apply or Nominate Applications and nominations are managed through the official L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science platform . To submit an application or nomination, users must: Create or log in to an account on the official For Women in Science platform. Access the relevant International Awards programme when the call is open. Follow the application or nomination instructions provided through the platform. Submit all required information and supporting documentation before the applicable deadline. If a user is logged into the platform but cannot access the form, the programme advises consulting the “How do I apply for a program?” section of its FAQ. Applicants and nominators should also review the official 2027 Rules and Regulations before preparing a submission. APPLY HERE Important Dates The official calendar for the 2027 L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards in Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science is: 6 April 2026: Call for applications/nominations opened 5 July 2026: Call for applications/nominations closed 31 December 2026: Final selection of candidates Because the submission deadline was 5 July 2026 , the nomination/application period for the 2027 International Awards is now closed. Those interested in future editions should continue monitoring the official For Women in Science platform for the next call. Important Clarification The L Oréal-UNESCO International Awards should not be confused with regional For Women in Science Fellowships or Young Talents programmes . The International Awards: Recognise five eminent women scientists globally Provide €100,000 to each laureate Focus on different scientific disciplines in alternating years Are intended to honour significant, established scientific achievement Regional fellowships may have different deadlines, eligibility requirements, award amounts and career-stage requirements. For this reason, information relating to a 31 August 2026 deadline for a Sub-Saharan Africa fellowship should not be applied to the 2027 International Awards described in this article. Why the L Oréal-UNESCO International Awards Matter Women continue to make groundbreaking contributions across mathematics, computing, physics and related scientific disciplines, yet their work has historically been underrepresented in some of the world s most prominent scientific awards and leadership structures. The L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards seek to increase the visibility of women researchers whose discoveries and ideas are helping push scientific boundaries forward. By recognising five exceptional scientists each year, the programme celebrates not simply individual achievement but also the broader importance of ensuring that women can participate, lead and receive recognition at the highest levels of international science. Final Thoughts The L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science International Awards 2027 represent a prestigious global recognition for exceptional women scientists working in Physical Sciences, Mathematics and Computer Science . Five laureates from five regions of the world will each receive €100,000 , recognising scientific achievements that have contributed substantially to the progress of research. The 2027 nomination cycle opened on 6 April 2026 and closed on 5 July 2026 , with final selections expected by 31 December 2026 . Researchers, universities, scientific institutions and potential nominators interested in future editions should monitor the official L Oréal-UNESCO For Women in Science platform for upcoming calls. title: University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship 2026: NZ$34,128 Annual Stipend and Tuition Fee Support for PhD Study in New Zealand
summary: The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is one of the University of Otago’s principal funding opportunities for students undertaking doctoral research in New Zealand. The scholarship supports academically outstanding candidates with strong research potential who are seeking to complete a PhD or an eligible professional doctorate at the University. For 2026, the scholarship provides a NZ$34,128 annual stipend , together with a tuition fee waiver at the domestic rate for up to 36 months of full-time doctoral study . The University indicates that up to 153 doctoral scholarships may be offered annually , making this one of its major postgraduate research funding programmes. Applications can be submitted throughout the year through the University of Otago’s eVision student portal . Rather than operating with one annual deadline, applications are considered through quarterly selection rounds in March, June, September and November . Applicants should note that the University of Otago is currently reviewing the strategic direction of its doctoral scholarship programme. Prospective candidates are therefore encouraged to check the official scholarship pages regularly for any changes to funding arrangements, eligibility or selection procedures. About the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is designed to support students undertaking supervised doctoral research at the University of Otago. Under the University’s postgraduate scholarship regulations, doctoral scholarships are awarded by the University Council on the recommendation of the Senate and are normally intended for candidates seeking their first doctoral qualification . A candidate may receive only one University of Otago doctoral scholarship. The scholarship may support students undertaking: Doctor of Philosophy programmes DClinDent Doctor of Musical Arts Doctor of Business Administration Doctor of Education Other eligible doctoral pathways covered by University regulations The scholarship is highly competitive. Selection is based predominantly on academic performance, research potential and the assessment of the academic department in which the candidate intends to undertake research. Scholarship Value For full-time doctoral students, the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship provides: NZ$34,128 per year as a living stipend plus: A tuition fee waiver at the domestic tuition-fee rate for up to 36 months The postgraduate research scholarship regulations confirm that the standard full-time doctoral scholarship emolument for 2026 is NZ$34,128 , normally paid in monthly instalments once the recipient is fully enrolled. For professional doctorates such as the DClinDent, DMA, DBA and EdD, the scholarship similarly provides a NZ$34,128 annual stipend and a tuition fee waiver for up to 36 months, although the tuition waiver is capped at the domestic rate. Students remain responsible for costs not covered by the tuition waiver, including applicable student services fees, insurance and other charges. The regulations specifically state that the scholarship covers the tuition component and that recipients may still be invoiced for remaining fees. Number of Scholarships Available The University states that up to: 153 University of Otago Doctoral Scholarships may be offered annually. Availability remains subject to institutional funding decisions and scholarship programme arrangements. The University is currently reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme, so future scholarship numbers, selection systems or funding arrangements may change. Applicants should always confirm the latest information on the University of Otago website before submitting an application. Who Can Apply? The scholarship primarily supports candidates seeking their first doctoral qualification. Applicants will normally need to demonstrate: Excellent previous academic performance Strong potential for research Appropriate preparation for doctoral-level study Admission eligibility for the proposed University of Otago doctoral programme A research topic that can be appropriately supervised at the University Confirmation of a doctoral scholarship is dependent on the candidate being approved for admission to the relevant doctoral programme and successfully completing the enrolment process. Can International Students Apply? International PhD candidates should pay particular attention to the University’s fee-status rules. The current regulations state that, unless otherwise specified, doctoral and research master’s scholarships are open to Domestic Fee Paying Students . However, the same regulations note that international students undertaking PhD study in New Zealand have been eligible to pay domestic PhD tuition fees under New Zealand policy. The University’s scholarship information consequently describes the main University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship as available to both domestic and international PhD candidates. International candidates for professional doctorates may also apply, but where they receive a scholarship, the tuition waiver is limited to the domestic fee rate. Any difference between the domestic-rate waiver and applicable international tuition fees would remain the student’s responsibility. Because the University is currently reviewing doctoral scholarship arrangements, international applicants should check their precise eligibility and fee status before relying on scholarship funding. How Candidates Are Selected The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship is awarded primarily on the basis of academic merit and research potential. The postgraduate scholarship regulations identify several factors considered during assessment. 1. Academic Record The University examines the applicant’s previous academic results. For candidates who have completed a master’s degree combining coursework and a substantial thesis, relevant advanced-level papers and thesis grades may be considered. Where a candidate does not have a master’s degree containing a thesis, the University may consider advanced-level papers from the applicant’s most relevant qualification. For applicants whose qualifications were obtained outside the University of Otago, the University calculates an appropriate GPA using relevant academic transcripts. 2. Research Potential The applicant’s potential for research, or an existing record of research achievement, is an important component of the assessment. Relevant evidence may include: Previous thesis research Research projects Academic publications Conference participation Research assistantships Relevant professional research Evidence demonstrating the ability to conduct independent academic work 3. Departmental Recommendation The advice, recommendation or ranking of the relevant Head of Department is also considered. This makes academic fit important. A strong scholarship application is not simply a collection of high grades. Candidates should also demonstrate that their proposed research fits the expertise and research environment available within the intended department. 4. Academic Division Priorities The strategic research and institutional priorities of the Academic Division supervising the proposed research may also influence selection. Duration of the Scholarship A full-time doctoral scholarship normally has a maximum tenure of: Three years or until the thesis is submitted, whichever occurs first. Continuation of funding is dependent on satisfactory annual progress reports from the department in which the student is registered. For candidates who have already completed at least two months of doctoral registration at the time the scholarship is awarded, the total funding period may be reduced accordingly. Full-Time and Part-Time Study University regulations allow postgraduate research scholarships to be held on either a full-time or approved part-time basis. Part-time arrangements are generally considered where full-time study is not practically possible and the candidate can demonstrate appropriate preparation for part-time doctoral research. Approved reasons for moving from full-time to part-time study can include: Health circumstances Significant caregiving responsibilities Certain career-related circumstances For approved part-time doctoral scholarship recipients, the scholarship period is generally extended while the annual stipend is reduced proportionally. The standard 2026 part-time doctoral scholarship emolument identified in the regulations is NZ$17,064 per year. Where Scholarship Recipients Study During the scholarship period, doctoral candidates are normally expected to undertake their research at: University of Otago, Dunedin University of Otago, Christchurch University of Otago, Wellington Exceptions may be approved where the research requires access to overseas facilities or opportunities that are essential to the project. Overseas doctoral scholarship tenure is not normally permitted automatically, although approval may be granted for particular research circumstances. Employment While Holding the Scholarship Full-time doctoral scholarship recipients are permitted to undertake some paid employment, but limits apply. Under the regulations, full-time scholarship recipients may not normally accept more than 500 hours of paid employment over a 12-month period without prior approval from the Scholarships and Prizes Committee. Part-time scholarship recipients have a corresponding maximum of 1,000 hours over 12 months without prior permission. Students must ensure that outside work does not interfere with satisfactory progress on their doctorate. University of Otago employees undertaking their doctoral qualification as part of their employment are not eligible for University of Otago scholarship funding under the general regulations. Other Scholarships and Additional Funding The University of Otago offers a wider range of specialised doctoral funding opportunities in addition to the principal University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship. Examples include: University of Otago Māori Doctoral Scholarship This scholarship is specifically available to Māori doctoral candidates. University of Otago Pacific Islands Doctoral Scholarship This funding is reserved for doctoral students of indigenous Pacific Island descent. University of Otago China Scholarship Council Doctoral Scholarship This pathway is available to eligible PhD candidates supported by the China Scholarship Council under the University’s institutional arrangements. The regulations indicate that this scholarship can include tuition support for up to four years and supplementary stipend support designed to bring the recipient’s stipend to the equivalent value of the standard University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship. University of Otago City of Literature PhD Scholarship This specialised opportunity supports a PhD candidate whose research focuses on literature. University of Otago Special Health Research Scholarship This programme supports outstanding graduate students planning careers in health research. Candidates from different academic disciplines may be considered where the proposed PhD research relates to human health. Other specialised scholarships exist in areas including economics, education, geology, chemistry, experimental science, cancer research and women’s postgraduate research. Applicants should therefore explore both the general University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship and any discipline-specific scholarship for which they may qualify. How to Apply Applications for University of Otago doctoral scholarships are completed online through the eVision student portal . The general process is: Apply for admission to an eligible doctoral programme at the University of Otago. Complete the required doctoral admission information. Once the admission application is sufficiently complete, an invitation to apply for a scholarship will appear through eVision. Complete and submit the scholarship application. Ensure that the relevant academic department completes its assessment. Wait for consideration in the appropriate scholarship selection round. The regulations confirm that applications are submitted online and that candidates receive the scholarship invitation after completing the relevant qualification admission application. Application Deadline and Quarterly Selection Rounds There is no single annual closing date for the University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship. Applications may be made throughout the year. Scholarship applications are currently considered in quarterly rounds held in: March June September November Applications must be submitted through eVision and have a completed departmental assessment by the first day of the relevant round month . Therefore, for applicants preparing applications in August 2026, the next practical assessment point is the September 2026 round , for which the application and departmental assessment should be complete by 1 September 2026 . Candidates who cannot complete the necessary requirements in time can prepare for the November round instead. International Academic Qualifications Applicants who completed their previous qualifications outside New Zealand or Australia may be required to undergo academic credential assessment depending on the country and qualification concerned. The University reserves the right to request an external evaluation of international academic qualifications. However, the scholarship regulations clarify that an external Education Credential Evaluators assessment is not necessarily required simply to establish scholarship eligibility, although it may be required separately by the University’s International Office for admission purposes. International applicants should therefore distinguish carefully between: Doctoral admission requirements, and Scholarship assessment requirements Both processes may involve different documentation. Reapplying for the Scholarship University of Otago doctoral scholarships are highly competitive, and scholarship selection decisions are normally final. However, candidates may request permission to reapply if they have significant new material that strengthens their original application. Examples could include: New academic results Additional research publications Significant new research experience New evidence of academic achievement Candidates seeking permission to reapply should contact the University of Otago Scholarships Office and provide their name, student ID and evidence of the new material. Important Funding Review Prospective applicants should be aware that the University of Otago has announced that it is reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme . The current scholarship information remains available, but candidates planning future doctoral study should monitor the official University website for updates. This is particularly important for applicants planning to begin their doctorate in a later academic period, since scholarship values, allocation mechanisms, eligibility or selection procedures could change. Contact Information For questions relating to postgraduate scholarships, applicants can contact: University of Otago Scholarships Office Email: scholarships@otago.ac.nz Telephone: 0800 80 80 98 Applicants should also consult the official University of Otago scholarship pages for the latest information on doctoral funding and specialised scholarship opportunities. Conclusion The University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship 2026 provides significant financial support for high-achieving doctoral candidates seeking to undertake research at one of New Zealand’s leading universities. With a NZ$34,128 annual stipend , a domestic-rate tuition fee waiver for up to three years and up to 153 scholarships potentially offered annually , the programme represents an important funding route for prospective PhD researchers. Applications can be submitted throughout the year through eVision and are assessed in quarterly rounds in March, June, September and November. Selection is strongly based on academic merit, research potential, departmental recommendation and alignment with the University’s research priorities. International PhD applicants may also be eligible, subject to doctoral admission and applicable domestic-fee status arrangements, while international professional doctorate candidates should pay particular attention to the domestic-rate cap on tuition support. Because the University is currently reviewing its doctoral scholarship programme, applicants should verify the latest funding arrangements before applying. For more information and to apply, visit the official University of Otago Doctoral Scholarship website . To discover more global scholarship opportunities, VISIT HERE . title: University of Strathclyde Unorthodox Health Activism in Britain After 1948 PhD Studentship 2027
summary: The University of Strathclyde is inviting applications for a postgraduate research opportunity exploring the history of unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948 . The three-year PhD research project offers an opportunity for a prospective doctoral researcher to investigate alternative approaches to health, grassroots activism, community organising and the experiences of people who participated in health movements outside mainstream medical practices. The project is particularly relevant to applicants interested in history, healthcare history, public health, social movements, complementary and alternative medicine, health policy, medical humanities, community activism, oral history, and the social history of medicine . The successful applicant will undertake independent doctoral research while working with academic supervisors in the University of Strathclyde s History subject area. The research will also be affiliated with a wider Wellcome-funded research project examining the transnational history of AIDS denial. The studentship provides Home fees and a stipend for three years , with study expected to commence on 1 January 2027 . Opportunity Overview The University of Strathclyde s PhD project, titled Unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948, seeks to develop a deeper historical understanding of alternative and unconventional approaches to health in Britain from the establishment of the National Health Service in 1948 through the late 20th and early 21st centuries. The research recognises that health activism outside mainstream medicine has played an important role in British society for decades. Although alternative health movements became particularly visible during the COVID-19 pandemic, debates around alternative medicine, health autonomy, medical authority, patient rights, and community-based approaches to well-being have a much longer history. The project therefore provides an opportunity to investigate how individuals and communities engaged with unconventional approaches to health, why they became involved, how these movements shaped everyday experiences of health, and how governments, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and public health practitioners responded. Key Details of the PhD Studentship University: University of Strathclyde Faculty: Humanities and Social Sciences Subject: History Programme: PhD History Research project: Unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948 Study mode: Full-time Duration: 3 years Number of places: 1 Opening date: 30 July 2026 Application deadline: 30 October 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Expected start date: 1 January 2027 Funding: Home tuition fees plus stipend Stipend for January 2027 starters: £16,354, based on the pro-rata equivalent of £21,805 Monthly stipend: Approximately £1,817 Stipend: Tax-free and paid monthly Supervisors: Dr Hannah Elizabeth and Professor Matthew Smith About the Research Project The research project examines the history of health movements that challenged or operated outside conventional medical approaches in Britain. Since the founding of the NHS in 1948, various grassroots organisations, activists, and communities have questioned established approaches to medicine and healthcare. These movements have included campaigns around alternative medicine, patient autonomy, mental health reform, nutrition, community healthcare, and other forms of health activism. The PhD will investigate these developments historically, asking not only what these movements believed but also what it meant to participate in them. Among the central questions the project seeks to explore are the following: What was it like to participate in unorthodox health movements? How did individuals become involved in alternative health communities? What motivated people to challenge mainstream medical practices? How did membership of health movements affect people s everyday experiences of health? How did health activists organise within local communities? What role did media representations play in shaping perceptions of alternative health? How did public health practitioners respond to these movements? How did healthcare workers and policymakers respond to challenges from health activists? How did alternative health movements evolve from the post-war period to the present? What impact did these movements have on broader understandings of health and medicine? These questions make the studentship particularly suitable for researchers who want to examine health not simply as a medical issue but as a social, cultural, political, and historical phenomenon . Suggested Research Areas Although applicants are encouraged to develop their own research programme, the University has identified several possible areas of focus. 1. The History of the British Anti-Vaccination Movement One possible area is the historical development of the anti-vaccination movement in Britain during the late 20th century and beyond. A project in this area could examine how opposition to vaccination developed, how activists organised themselves, the arguments they presented, the communities they built, and the ways in which government and public health institutions responded. The research could also examine how historical anti-vaccination activism influenced later debates around vaccination and public health. 2. Cancer Denial Another potential research area is the history of cancer denial. This could involve investigating individuals or communities that rejected conventional understandings of cancer, questioned established cancer treatments or promoted alternative explanations and treatments. Such research could examine the relationship between medical authority, patient experiences, alternative health beliefs and public communication. 3. Complementary and Alternative Medicine The project also welcomes research into Complementary and Alternative Medicine (CAM) and its relationship with everyday health. Researchers could examine the development and popularity of practices such as herbal medicine, homeopathy, naturopathy, and other forms of complementary healthcare. A project could investigate why people turned to these approaches, how practitioners developed their communities, and how CAM interacted with the NHS and conventional healthcare. 4. Media Representations of Alternative Health Movements Media and communications provide another potentially important area of study. A PhD could explore how newspapers, television, radio, magazines, digital media, and other communication channels represented alternative health movements. This could include examining whether media coverage contributed to the growth of particular movements, reinforced public concerns, or shaped perceptions of alternative healthcare. 5. Regional Unorthodox Health Activism Applicants may also consider focusing on health activism in particular regions of Britain. A regional study could reveal how local histories, communities, social conditions, and healthcare provisions influenced the development of alternative health movements. This approach could be especially valuable for understanding how national debates around health translated into local activism. 6. Spiritual and Religious Health Communities Another potential research direction is the relationship between health activism and spiritual or religious communities. This could examine communities that developed alternative understandings of health and well-being based on spiritual, religious, or philosophical beliefs. Researchers could explore how these communities organised, how members understood health and illness, and how their practices interacted with mainstream medical institutions. 7. The History of Wellness Movements The project also provides an opportunity to study the emergence and development of modern wellness movements. A research project could investigate how ideas about well-being, lifestyle, nutrition, fitness, self-care, and personal responsibility evolved over time. It could also explore the historical relationship between wellness culture and broader changes in healthcare, consumer culture, media, and society. Connection to a Wider Wellcome-Funded Research Project The studentship will be affiliated with the Wellcome-funded project A Transnational History of AIDS Denial: Origins, Manifestations, and Persistence, 1981 to the present. This connection creates an opportunity for the doctoral researcher to situate their work within a wider scholarly investigation into unconventional approaches to health and medicine. Applicants whose proposed research examines similar forms of unorthodox health activity during the 20th and/or 21st centuries are particularly encouraged to apply. The relationship between the studentship and the wider project may also provide a valuable intellectual environment for exploring questions concerning health beliefs, medical authority, activism, public communication, and historical change. Funding and Financial Support One of the major attractions of this PhD opportunity is the financial support attached to the studentship. The award covers Home tuition fees and provides a stipend for the duration of the three-year programme. For candidates commencing study on 1 January 2027 , the stated stipend is £16,354 , described by the University as the pro-rata equivalent of the £21,805 rate. The stipend is expected to be paid in monthly installments of approximately £1,817 and is tax-free. The stipend is also likely to increase each year, subject to the applicable funding arrangements. The funding is intended to support the successful doctoral researcher throughout the three-year period of study, provided the programme is completed within the funded duration. Applicants should carefully review the University s funding conditions and fee arrangements before applying, particularly where international fee differences may apply. Academic Supervision The successful doctoral researcher will be supervised by academics in the University of Strathclyde s History subject area. The listed supervisory team includes: Dr Hannah Elizabeth Research Fellow, History Professor Matthew Smith Professor, History Applicants are required to contact the supervisory team before submitting their formal application. This preliminary discussion is an important part of the application process because applicants need to ensure that their proposed research aligns with the themes and objectives of the studentship. Application Process Applicants must complete two important stages. Step 1: Contact the Supervisory Team Before submitting the formal application, applicants should contact one of the following: Dr Hannah Elizabeth at hannah.elizabeth@strath.ac.uk Professor Matt Smith at m.smith@strath.ac.uk Applicants should introduce their proposed research ideas and discuss how their project relates to the themes of the studentship. This stage is important because the University wants applicants to demonstrate that their research proposal is compatible with the project s focus before submitting the formal application. Step 2: Submit the Formal PhD Application After engaging with the supervisory team, applicants should submit an online application through the University s Pegasus application system for PhD History . The application should specify the start date of 1 January 2027 . In the funding section of the application form, applicants should enter the project title: Unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948. Required Application Documents Applicants must prepare a complete application containing all required supporting documents. 1. 1,000-Word Research Proposal The research proposal should be approximately 1,000 words and explain the research the applicant intends to undertake over the three years of the PhD. Applicants may propose either: one central research project; or several closely related case studies. The proposal should demonstrate a clear understanding of the historical subject, establish the research questions, and explain the proposed approach to investigating unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948. Applicants should also ensure they have completed the first application step and contacted the supervisory team before submitting the proposal. 2. 500-Word Personal Statement Applicants must submit a 500-word personal statement explaining why they want to undertake the studentship. The statement should provide a clear explanation of the applicant s academic motivation and interest in the proposed area of research. It should also demonstrate why the applicant is well suited to doctoral research in this field. 3. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a CV of up to three pages . The CV should clearly present relevant academic qualifications, research experience, publications where applicable, professional experience, and other achievements relevant to doctoral study. 4. Two Academic References Applicants must provide two academic references . The references should include the referees names and full contact details. 5. Degree Certificates and Transcripts Applicants must provide copies of all degree certificates and academic transcripts obtained to date. These documents should allow the University to assess the applicant s academic background and eligibility. 6. English Language Evidence Where English is not the applicant s first language, the application should include evidence of English-language proficiency. The University specifies IELTS Academic , taken within the two years preceding commencement of study, or an equivalent accepted English-language qualification. Applicants should ensure that their language evidence meets the University s requirements. APPLY HERE Application Deadline The deadline for applications is: 30 October 2026 at 5:00 PM BST Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final hours to submit their applications. Because the University states that incomplete applications will not be considered, applicants should allow sufficient time to upload every required document and verify that their application is complete. Important Warning About Generative AI The University of Strathclyde explicitly addresses the use of generative artificial intelligence in its application guidance. Applicants are advised that their research proposals should be written in their own words . The University notes that generative AI tools can produce inaccurate or outdated information and that academics may be able to identify text generated using such tools. For a doctoral application, this is particularly important because the research proposal is intended to demonstrate the applicant s own academic ability, research skills, critical thinking, and capacity to develop a viable PhD project. Applicants should therefore use appropriate academic research practices and ensure that their proposal genuinely represents their own thinking, research interests, and academic writing abilities. Selection and Interview Process After the application deadline, applications will be reviewed and ranked by a selection panel. Only complete applications will be considered. Applicants who are shortlisted for an interview are expected to be notified in early to mid-November 2026 . Interviews will take place online during the week beginning 23 November 2026 . An important feature of the process is that interview questions will be provided to shortlisted candidates in advance. This gives shortlisted applicants an opportunity to prepare carefully for the interview and reflect on their proposed research, academic background, and motivation for pursuing the PhD. The successful applicant must be able to begin their doctoral studies on 1 January 2027 . How to Develop a Strong Application Competition for funded doctoral studentships can be significant, so applicants should approach the application strategically. Develop a Focused Research Question Rather than attempting to investigate every form of alternative health activism in Britain, applicants should develop a manageable research focus. A strong proposal should establish a clear historical problem and explain why that problem deserves further research. Demonstrate Historical Significance Applicants should explain why their proposed topic matters historically. For example, a proposal could examine how alternative health movements changed relationships between patients and medical professionals, contributed to debates about healthcare policy or influenced public understandings of health. Connect the Research to the Studentship Themes The proposed project should clearly relate to unorthodox approaches to health, activism, community organisation or alternative medical practices. Applicants should demonstrate that they understand the purpose of the studentship rather than submitting a generic history research proposal. Consider Primary Sources Because the project encourages archival research and oral history, applicants should think carefully about the types of primary sources that could support their research. Potential sources could include archival records, newspapers, campaign materials, organisational documents, personal accounts, oral histories, media coverage, and other historical records. The specific sources will depend on the proposed research question. Demonstrate Originality A competitive PhD proposal should go beyond simply describing an existing movement. Applicants should identify an aspect of the topic that could contribute something new to historical scholarship. The research proposal should therefore demonstrate curiosity, analytical thinking, and a clear understanding of the potential contribution of the research. Contact the Supervisors Early Applicants should not overlook the requirement to contact the supervisory team before submitting the formal application. Early communication can help applicants refine their research ideas and ensure that their proposed project fits the available supervision and wider research themes. Why This PhD Opportunity Is Significant The project provides an opportunity to study the relationship between medicine, society, activism, and individual experiences of health. Unorthodox health movements can reveal important historical questions about trust in medical institutions, patient autonomy, public health communication, healthcare inequality, and the ways people seek information and support outside conventional systems. The project is also particularly timely because debates around alternative medicine, vaccination, wellness, medical authority, and health information have become increasingly prominent in contemporary society. By placing these debates within a longer historical context, doctoral research can help explain where these movements came from, how they developed, and why they continue to influence discussions about health. Potential Career and Academic Benefits A three-year PhD at the University of Strathclyde can provide extensive research and academic development. The successful researcher will have the opportunity to develop skills in areas such as the following: Historical research Archival research Oral history Qualitative research Critical analysis Academic writing Research design Interview techniques Analysis of social movements Health and medical history Public health history Historical interpretation Presentation of research findings Independent project management These skills can be valuable for careers in academia, research, museums and archives, public policy, heritage, healthcare research, public history, communications, education, and other research-intensive sectors. Visit HERE for more information about the University of Strathclyde Unorthodox Health Activism in Britain After 1948 PhD Studentship 2027 opportunity. Important Dates Applicants should keep the following dates in mind: 30 July 2026: Applications open 30 October 2026 at 5:00 PM BST: Application deadline Early to mid-November 2026: Shortlisted applicants expected to be notified Week beginning 23 November 2026: Online interviews 1 January 2027: Expected commencement of the PhD Final Application Checklist Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should make sure they have completed every required stage. Contact the supervisory team with research proposal ideas. Confirm that the proposed project aligns with the studentship themes. Prepare a 1,000-word research proposal. Prepare a 500-word personal statement. Prepare a CV of no more than three pages. Arrange two academic references with full contact details. Upload all degree certificates and academic transcripts. Provide IELTS Academic or an accepted equivalent where required. Select PhD History through the University s online application system. Select the start date of 1 January 2027. Enter Unorthodox health activism in Britain after 1948 in the funding section. Check that every required document has been uploaded. Submit the complete application before 5:00 PM BST on 30 October 2026. Conclusion The University of Strathclyde Unorthodox Health Activism in Britain after 1948 PhD Studentship 2027 presents a distinctive opportunity for doctoral researchers interested in the history of medicine, health activism, alternative healthcare, and grassroots movements in Britain. The project goes beyond conventional medical history by examining the experiences of individuals and communities that challenged established approaches to healthcare. Through archival research and oral history, the successful researcher will have the opportunity to investigate how alternative health movements emerged, how people became involved in them and how these movements influenced everyday experiences of health and interactions with medical institutions. With three years of funding, Home tuition fees, and a tax-free stipend , the studentship offers substantial financial support for doctoral study. The connection to a wider Wellcome-funded research project also provides an important research context for investigating unconventional approaches to health during the 20th and 21st centuries. Prospective applicants should begin preparing early, particularly because they are required to contact the supervisory team before submitting their formal application. A carefully developed research proposal, a strong academic record, complete supporting documentation, and a clear explanation of the project s historical significance will be important components of a competitive application. The application deadline is 30 October 2026 at 5:00 PM BST , and the successful candidate is expected to commence the PhD on 1 January 2027 .
