title: University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship 2026: NZ$33,000 Annual Stipend, Tuition Fees and PhD Funding in New Zealand
summary: The University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship 2026 provides substantial financial support for high-achieving students undertaking doctoral research at the University of Waikato in New Zealand. Open to eligible domestic and international students , the scholarship offers a living allowance of up to NZ$33,000 per year for as long as 36 months , together with domestic doctoral tuition fees and the University’s Student Services Fee. Established in 1996 to promote excellence in postgraduate research, the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship supports candidates who have demonstrated strong academic achievement, research readiness and the potential to make a meaningful contribution through advanced research. The number of scholarships awarded each year is not fixed and depends on the funding available. The scholarship covers a wide range of research areas, including arts, business and management, computer science, mathematics, education, health, engineering, law, Māori and Indigenous studies, science, social sciences and environmental studies. Applications are considered in four scholarship rounds each year . The official closing dates are 31 January, 30 April, 31 July and 31 October . As of August 2026, the next application deadline is therefore 31 October 2026 . About the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship The University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship was established to provide financial assistance to outstanding candidates who have received an Offer of Place for an approved higher research degree at the University. The scholarship is not simply awarded on the basis of admission to a doctoral programme. Candidates must separately demonstrate strong academic credentials, readiness to undertake independent research and the potential for their proposed research to generate meaningful academic or wider societal impact. The University considers applications in four competitive rounds each year rather than continuously awarding scholarships as applications arrive. Selection panels normally meet in: Early March Early June Early September Early December Applications are not considered outside these scheduled rounds. Scholarship Value The standard University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship provides a substantial package of financial support. Successful recipients may receive: NZ$33,000 living allowance per year Monthly stipend payments Funding for up to 36 months Domestic tuition fees for the eligible doctoral programme University Student Services Fee The standard living allowance totals NZ$33,000 for every 12 months and is normally paid in monthly instalments for up to three years. For approved part-time students, the living allowance is paid on a proportional basis. The Scholarships Executive may also offer a fees-only scholarship in some circumstances. A fees-only award normally covers domestic tuition fees and the Student Services Fee but does not include the NZ$33,000 annual living allowance. Costs Not Covered by the Scholarship Applicants should be aware that the scholarship does not necessarily cover every expense associated with studying in New Zealand. Recipients are responsible for finding other sources of funding for additional costs such as: Medical or health insurance Relocation and moving expenses Research-related expenses not otherwise funded Personal living costs exceeding the stipend Other miscellaneous expenses The official regulations explicitly state that medical insurance, moving costs and research expenses must be met through other means. International applicants should therefore prepare a realistic financial plan rather than assuming the scholarship eliminates all costs associated with doctoral study. Duration of the Scholarship The maximum scholarship tenure is: 36 months, or three years, of full-time doctoral enrolment. Part-time arrangements may extend the calendar duration of the scholarship, but the value and duration are adjusted proportionally. For candidates entering the Doctor of Health Science, Doctor of Musical Arts or Doctor of Juridical Science, scholarship tenure begins when the student commences Part 1 of the relevant doctoral programme. If the recipient submits their thesis, withdraws from the doctoral programme or otherwise ends their doctoral enrolment before the end of the scholarship period, scholarship payments also end. Who Can Apply? The scholarship is available to a broad range of applicants, including New Zealand and international students. According to the 2026 scholarship regulations, eligible applicants may include: New Zealand citizens New Zealand permanent residents New Zealand Resident Class Visa holders Australian citizens or permanent residents domiciled in New Zealand International students This means the scholarship is genuinely available to qualified candidates from outside New Zealand. However, nationality alone does not determine eligibility. Applicants must satisfy several important academic and procedural requirements. Eligible Doctoral Programmes Applicants must hold an Offer of Place in an eligible doctoral qualification at the University of Waikato. The scholarship regulations specifically identify: Doctor of Philosophy Doctor of Health Science Doctor of Musical Arts Doctor of Juridical Science Applicants must not have commenced enrolment in the eligible degree before the closing date of the scholarship round in which they are being considered, subject to the detailed timing provisions in the regulations. Important Note for Doctor of Education Applicants Although the University offers the Doctor of Education , the principal University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship regulations treat EdD candidates differently. The regulations note that candidates enrolling in an EdD may instead apply for the University of Waikato Taught Postgraduate Scholarship for Part 1 and the Doctoral Catalyst Scholarship for Part 2. Applicants interested specifically in the EdD should therefore check the appropriate funding route rather than assuming they qualify for the standard Doctoral Scholarship described here. Academic Requirements Admission to higher research degree study generally requires a strong academic foundation. Prospective candidates would normally be expected to have completed: A Bachelor’s degree with Honours, or A Master’s degree The qualifying degree must include a significant research component . According to the University’s doctoral admissions process, the research component normally needs to consist of a thesis, dissertation or research project representing at least 25% of one year of the qualifying degree. Research-methods courses alone do not count as the required research component. Applicants must also normally have achieved at least a Second Class, First Division result in the qualification used for doctoral admission. Scholarship Academic Standard The scholarship itself is more competitive than simply meeting the minimum doctoral admission requirements. The 2026 regulations specify that candidates normally require a minimum: GPA of A- calculated from the qualification being used for entry to the doctoral programme. Having an A- GPA does not guarantee a scholarship. It establishes the minimum academic threshold within the scholarship selection framework. Additional Selection Criteria The University considers more than grades. Other factors can include: Previous research experience Professional experience relevant to the proposed research Readiness to undertake independent research Academic references Research publications Capacity of the supervisory panel to support the project Alignment with University, Faculty, School or Research Institute priorities Understanding of Mātauranga Māori and Pacific knowledges where relevant Potential contribution to sustainable development Wider impact of the proposed research The regulations specifically note that selection may consider alignment with institutional research priorities and the potential for research to generate impact, including advancement of the Sustainable Development Goals. Who Is Not Eligible? Applicants are considered ineligible if they: Already hold a doctoral degree or equivalent qualification Do not have an Offer of Place by the relevant scholarship-round deadline Have already been considered twice for the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship Candidates who have not yet obtained an Offer of Place when a round closes may apply again in a subsequent round if they continue to meet all other requirements. Candidates are therefore allowed a maximum of two scholarship selection attempts . If unsuccessful in their first round, they may apply once more. Step 1: Check Your Eligibility for Doctoral Study Before thinking about the scholarship itself, candidates should determine whether they meet the academic requirements for their chosen University of Waikato research degree. The University offers higher research qualifications including: Doctor of Philosophy Doctor of Health Science Doctor of Education Doctor of Musical Arts Doctor of Juridical Science Master of Philosophy Applicants should carefully review the regulations for the specific programme they are considering because individual research degrees may have additional requirements. International candidates must also satisfy the University s applicable English-language requirements. Step 2: Find a University of Waikato Supervisor A major feature of the University of Waikato doctoral application process is that applicants must identify an appropriate supervisor before submitting the formal application . Prospective students should explore University staff profiles and identify researchers whose interests align with the proposed doctoral topic. Potential supervisors can be searched according to factors such as: Research interests Publications Previous doctoral supervision Availability to supervise Current projects Applicants should then contact appropriate academics directly to discuss the proposed research and its alignment with the supervisor s expertise. Step 3: Obtain an Invitation to Apply A prospective supervisor must formally agree to supervise the candidate before the doctoral application can progress. Once agreement has been reached, the University of Waikato supervisor will provide the prospective applicant with an: Invitation to Apply This step is essential. Candidates who do not possess an Invitation to Apply will not have their doctoral application considered. Applicants should therefore avoid approaching the doctoral admissions process as though they can simply submit an online form first and look for a supervisor afterward. Step 4: Prepare Your Application Documents After receiving the Invitation to Apply, candidates should prepare all documentation required for the Application to Enrol. Applicants need to identify at least one University of Waikato supervisor who has agreed to supervise them. They must also provide contact information for: Two academic referees who are willing to be contacted as part of the doctoral admissions process. Candidates should carefully check the University’s PhD and Higher Research Degree Application Checklist before submitting. Step 5: Submit the Application to Enrol Applications are submitted through the University’s MyWaikato Application Portal . Candidates upload the required academic and supporting documents, provide evidence of their supervisor’s Invitation to Apply and enter their referees’ contact details. Doctoral admission applications are normally considered monthly between February and November . The University’s School or Faculty reviews each complete application before it proceeds through the institutional approval process. Step 6: Apply for the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship Scholarship applications are linked to the doctoral enrolment process. The scholarship cannot be applied for as an entirely separate standalone opportunity. The regulations state that applications are submitted as part of the application to enrol in a doctoral programme. When applying through MyWaikato, candidates can provide additional information specifically supporting their scholarship case. What You Need to Include in the Scholarship Application The 2026 application asks candidates to provide several research-focused statements. Proposed Thesis Information Applicants must confirm: Their proposed thesis title Their approved Chief Supervisor Academic and Research Preparation Candidates must explain how their academic background, research experience and relevant professional experience have prepared them to undertake the proposed doctoral project. Applicants are encouraged to provide specific examples rather than broad claims. Contribution of the Research Applicants must describe how the project will: Advance knowledge, or Influence practice in the relevant field They should explain why the proposed contribution is timely and significant. The University encourages applicants to identify the knowledge gap or problem their research addresses. Mātauranga Māori, Pacific Knowledges and Te Tiriti o Waitangi Applicants are asked to explain whether their research connects with: Mātauranga Māori Pacific knowledges Te Tiriti o Waitangi principles and values Where research involves Māori or Pacific communities or data, applicants should describe appropriate engagement and data-governance practices. Broader Research Impact Candidates are also asked to reflect on the significance of their proposed research beyond academia. Potential impact can include contributions to: Society Economy Environment Health Culture Applicants should also discuss how they plan to engage with audiences that could use or benefit from the research. Career Aspirations Applicants must describe their career goals and explain how the doctoral research will help them achieve those goals. They should also identify skills and capabilities they hope to develop through doctoral study. References Scholarship applicants may submit up to two references. The scholarship application requires: One academic reference, mandatory This would normally come from someone familiar with the applicant’s previous academic study or research, often at the institution where the qualifying degree was completed. Applicants may additionally submit: One professional reference, optional The professional referee should ideally be familiar with employment or experience relevant to the proposed doctoral research. Scholarship Deadlines Applications are considered during four rounds each year. The official deadlines are: 31 January 30 April 31 July 31 October Since the current date is August 2026, the next available scholarship application deadline is 31 October 2026 . Applicants should not wait until the deadline to begin the process because they need to: Identify an appropriate research supervisor Contact the supervisor Secure agreement to supervision Obtain an Invitation to Apply Prepare documentation Submit the doctoral Application to Enrol Receive an Offer of Place Complete the scholarship application An Offer of Place must be received by the closing date of the relevant scholarship round. When Will Applicants Receive a Decision? Successful applicants are generally notified of their scholarship outcome within: Up to eight weeks after the relevant application deadline. Once offered the scholarship, recipients must accept it within 28 days , otherwise the offer lapses. Full-Time Study Expectations Recipients are normally expected to study full time. Full-time scholarship holders should undertake approximately: 37.5 hours of doctoral study per week They may take up to four weeks of annual holiday, excluding University and public holidays, without formally suspending the scholarship. Can Scholarship Holders Work? Yes, but employment restrictions apply. Full-time scholarship holders are normally limited to: 500 hours of paid employment per year. Applicants wanting to exceed this limit must obtain approval from the Scholarships Executive, and approval is generally reserved for exceptional circumstances. This arrangement is intended to ensure that doctoral research remains the recipient’s principal commitment. Part-Time Scholarship Arrangements Part-time scholarship tenure may be permitted where students have compelling personal circumstances such as: Illness Disability Parenting responsibilities Caring responsibilities Requests are considered individually. During approved part-time study, the scholarship amount, tenure and employment allowances are adjusted proportionally. Part-time status is not intended to allow recipients to undertake full-time employment while holding the doctoral scholarship. Can You Hold Another Scholarship at the Same Time? Certain smaller awards for research or conference purposes may be held alongside the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship. Generally, lower-value awards may be held where the combined value of other awards does not exceed 50% of the doctoral scholarship’s annual living allowance . Additional approval may be required where other funding exceeds this threshold. Recipients offered a scholarship from a government sponsoring body or University partner, such as a China Scholarship Council scholarship , would normally need to relinquish the University-funded scholarship unless permission for concurrent tenure is granted. Research Areas The scholarship can support doctoral research across a broad range of disciplines available at the University of Waikato. Potential fields include: Arts Business and Management Computer Science Mathematics Education Health Engineering Law Māori and Indigenous Studies Science Social Sciences Environmental Studies Applicants should identify a research topic that fits both their academic background and the expertise available among University of Waikato supervisors. Why Consider the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship? For prospective research students, the University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship combines three important forms of support: A substantial annual stipend Doctoral tuition support Structured institutional research supervision The scholarship also places substantial weight on research impact , not merely grades. Candidates are encouraged to show how their research could make a difference academically and beyond the University, whether through social, environmental, economic, cultural or health outcomes. This makes the scholarship particularly relevant to applicants capable of articulating not only what they intend to research, but why the research matters . Contact Information For enquiries relating to doctoral study and higher research degrees, applicants can contact: University of Waikato School of Graduate Research Telephone: +64 7 858 5096 Email: sgr@waikato.ac.nz Applicants should use the University s doctoral application process page for current admission instructions. Conclusion The University of Waikato Doctoral Scholarship 2026 is an attractive funding opportunity for high-achieving domestic and international candidates seeking advanced research training in New Zealand. The standard scholarship provides NZ$33,000 per year for up to 36 months , together with domestic doctoral tuition fees and the Student Services Fee. Applicants must normally demonstrate at least an A- GPA , strong independent research potential and a well-developed doctoral project. They must also secure an appropriate University of Waikato supervisor, receive an Invitation to Apply, submit a complete doctoral application and obtain an Offer of Place before the relevant scholarship round closes. Four application rounds are held each year, closing on 31 January, 30 April, 31 July and 31 October . For candidates applying after July 2026, the next deadline is 31 October 2026 . Because securing a supervisor and doctoral Offer of Place can take considerable time, prospective candidates should begin the process well before the scholarship deadline. For more information about doctoral study and applications at the University of Waikato, visit the official doctoral application page. title: Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil Studentships 2027: Fully Funded PhD Opportunities at the University of Oxford
summary: The Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research (OCEMR) DPhil Studentships 2027 offer an exceptional opportunity for prospective doctoral researchers who want to contribute to cutting-edge research focused on children and young people, neurodiversity, mental health, development, learning, and well-being. For the 2027 entry cycle, the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research is inviting expressions of interest from candidates interested in undertaking a DPhil at the University of Oxford from October 2027 . Thanks to generous funding from the Paul Foundation, up to four fully funded studentships are available. The funding package includes a stipend and fees for three years at the UK home-fee rate , with the funded studentships expected to be completed by October 2030. The opportunity is particularly relevant to researchers interested in understanding children s and young people s differences, strengths, development, and mental health, while contributing to research designed to promote more inclusive and supportive environments. According to the Department of Experimental Psychology, the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research focuses on conducting world-class research with children and young people, with the broader goal of creating a world in which differences are understood and accepted, individual strengths are recognised and developed, and mental health difficulties are prevented or addressed at an early stage. Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research DPhil Studentships 2027 The University of Oxford is one of the world s leading research universities, and the OCEMR provides an interdisciplinary research environment bringing together expertise relevant to child development, mental health, psychology, and related fields. The 2027 studentships are designed for candidates who want to pursue doctoral-level research within the Centre and contribute to research that has potential implications for children, young people, families, educators, and other stakeholders. The Centre s research agenda is particularly concerned with: Children and young people s development Mental health and well-being Neurodiversity Understanding individual differences Strengths-based approaches Learning and development Early identification and prevention of mental health difficulties Inclusive approaches to childhood and adolescence Research involving children, young people, and their families Interdisciplinary approaches to psychological and developmental research What Does the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Studentship 2027 Cover? One of the most attractive aspects of this opportunity is its funding package. The University of Oxford states that up to four fully funded OCEMR studentships will be offered for the October 2027 intake. Successful students will receive: A doctoral studentship for three years A stipend for living expenses University fees at the UK home-fee rate The opportunity to undertake doctoral research within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research Membership of an interdisciplinary research environment The opportunity to work alongside researchers with expertise in children, young people, psychology, education, and mental health The opportunity to contribute to research with potential practical and societal impact The funding is supported by the Paul Foundation . Important Note About the Funding Applicants should pay particular attention to the fact that the published funding is specified at the UK home-fee rate . This means applicants should carefully examine the University s graduate admissions and funding requirements to determine how their individual fee status affects the total financial support available to them. The department also notes that scholarship and grant opportunities for UK study can be highly competitive and may have specific nationality, course, or eligibility restrictions. Prospective applicants are therefore encouraged to check the detailed eligibility requirements before applying. Who Is the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Opportunity For? The opportunity is intended for prospective doctoral researchers who have a strong interest in research involving children and young people and whose academic interests align with the Centre s research priorities. Potential applicants may be particularly well-suited to the opportunity if their interests involve areas such as the following: Child development Adolescent development Psychology Mental health Neurodiversity Autism ADHD Learning and education Language and communication Executive functions and self-regulation Socio-emotional development Wellbeing Strengths-based approaches Inclusive research Assistive technology Artificial intelligence and its application to developmental or educational research Community-based participatory research Co-production with children, young people, families, and educators The opportunity is therefore broader than a conventional psychology PhD. The Centre s work brings together psychological, clinical, educational, and developmental perspectives, making it particularly attractive to candidates whose research interests cross disciplinary boundaries. Research Themes Within the Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research The Oxford Centre for Emerging Minds Research is focused on research that can improve understanding of children s and young people s experiences and support better developmental and mental health outcomes. Its work is centred around the principle that differences between people should be understood and accepted, while strengths should be recognised and supported. The Centre also aims to address mental health difficulties through prevention and early intervention rather than waiting until problems become more severe. This makes the DPhil opportunity especially relevant for researchers interested in research that connects academic investigation with real-world challenges affecting children, young people, and their communities. What Kind of Research Could Applicants Pursue? The source material indicates that applicants will be able to consider potential OCEMR DPhil projects and should consult the available project information when developing their expression of interest. The Centre s research direction includes work examining the following: How children s and young people s strengths can be identified and supported How differences in development influence learning and well-being How mental health difficulties can be prevented or addressed early How neurodivergent children and young people can be better supported How families and educators can contribute to research How research can incorporate the perspectives of children and young people How interdisciplinary methods can be used to address complex developmental questions Candidates should therefore avoid approaching the application as simply an opportunity to study a broad topic. A strong application should demonstrate a clear intellectual connection between the applicant s research interests and the Centre s research priorities. Why This DPhil Opportunity Is Significant A doctoral studentship at Oxford provides more than financial support. It provides an opportunity to develop advanced research expertise in an internationally recognised academic environment. For candidates interested in child development, mental health, psychology, neurodiversity, or related areas, the OCEMR provides an environment where research can be connected to broader questions concerning education, well-being, inclusion, and social development. The Centre s emphasis on interdisciplinary research can also allow doctoral researchers to engage with perspectives beyond a single academic discipline. Doctoral applications often require substantial preparation, including reviewing research projects, identifying academic fit and preparing supporting documents. How to Apply for the Oxford OCEMR DPhil Studentships 2027 The first stage is to submit an expression of interest for the OCEMR DPhil opportunity. The Department of Experimental Psychology provides information about potential OCEMR DPhil projects and separate guidance concerning the submission of an expression of interest. Prospective candidates should, therefore: Step 1: Review the Available Research Projects Begin by examining the available OCEMR DPhil projects. This is important because doctoral research at Oxford is expected to demonstrate a strong connection between the applicant s proposed interests and the academic expertise available within the department and research centre. Step 2: Assess Your Academic and Research Fit Consider whether your academic background, previous research experience, and proposed interests align with the Centre s areas of research. Applicants should be able to explain why the OCEMR is the appropriate environment for their doctoral research. Step 3: Develop a Clear Research Direction Your expression of interest should demonstrate intellectual curiosity and a clear understanding of the research area you want to investigate. Rather than presenting an extremely broad topic, applicants should identify a research direction that can realistically be developed into doctoral research. Step 4: Prepare the Required Application Materials Applicants should carefully follow the University s instructions concerning the expression of interest and submit the requested materials before the deadline. Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline The initial expression of interest must be submitted by: 12.00 noon, Tuesday, 22 September 2026. Although the source does not provide a single comprehensive checklist of all selection criteria for the 2027 OCEMR studentships, prospective candidates should demonstrate a strong alignment with the Centre s research agenda. A competitive applicant would ideally be able to demonstrate: Strong academic preparation Clear research interests Interest in children and young people Alignment with the Centre s research priorities An ability to think critically about research questions Potential to conduct independent doctoral research Interest in interdisciplinary research A commitment to research that can contribute to improved understanding of development, wellbeing or mental health A clear reason for wanting to undertake doctoral study at Oxford Previous research experience can also be valuable when demonstrating preparedness for doctoral-level study, although applicants should rely on the official admissions and studentship guidance for the precise requirements. International Applicants and Eligibility The available source does not state that the 2027 OCEMR studentships are restricted to a particular race, nationality, or continent. Identify the research themes that most closely match their academic interests. Review the University s graduate admissions requirements. Examine the relevant fee and funding conditions. Prepare a strong academic CV. Develop their research interests into a focused doctoral direction. Review any required supporting documents. Ensure that their application demonstrates a clear fit with the proposed research environment. Submit the expression of interest before the stated deadline. The Wider Funding Landscape at Oxford The Department of Experimental Psychology states that applicants who receive an offer are automatically considered for funding from a number of sources, including the Wellcome Trust, MRC, BBSRC, Cancer Research UK, ESRC, the British Heart Foundation, the Clarendon Fund, Oxford colleges, and various charitable sources. The department advises applicants seeking funding for its graduate courses to submit their university applications by the early December deadline. This broader funding landscape demonstrates why prospective students should investigate multiple funding routes rather than relying on a single studentship. Oxford also provides a funding search tool intended to help applicants identify scholarships, studentships, and awards for which they may be eligible. Career and Academic Benefits of a Funded DPhil Completing a funded DPhil at the University of Oxford can provide substantial academic and professional development. Potential benefits include the following: Advanced doctoral research training Development of specialist expertise Experience conducting independent research Exposure to interdisciplinary research Collaboration with researchers from different fields Opportunities to contribute to research publications and outputs Development of analytical and methodological skills Experience working on research involving children and young people Preparation for academic and research careers Development of expertise relevant to psychology, education, mental health, policy, and related fields Membership of an internationally recognised academic research environment For individuals pursuing careers in academia, research, public policy, education, mental health, or child development, this type of doctoral training can provide a strong foundation for future professional opportunities. Connect Your Interests to OCEMR Show how your proposed research connects with the Centre s work on children, young people, development, mental health, neurodiversity, and well-being. 3. Instead, identify the particular research problem, population, developmental stage, mechanism, or intervention that interests you. 6. Explain the Potential Contribution Consider what your research could add to existing knowledge and how it might ultimately contribute to children, young people, families, educators, or practitioners.
